ICE Shot Pepper Spray Into a Car in a Traffic Stop, Then Broke a Detainee’s Collarbone

A new federal lawsuit accuses ICE and DHS of a batch of brutal warrantless arrests.

Actual Article Body:
© THE INTERCEPT

ALL RIGHTS RESERVED

A new federal lawsuit accuses ICE and DHS of a batch of brutal warrantless arrests.

Jose Rosito Roca Estrada and his friends were on their way to work in a van on June 27, when a car in front of them slammed on its brakes, forcing them to crash into it and ricochet backward on the busy highway.

Three more cars surrounded theirs, and an estimated 10 to 12 officers poured out. The agents screamed at the men to get out of the vehicle despite traffic whipping by, Roca Estrada and fellow passenger Elvis Manuel Mejia told The Intercept. The stalemate ended with the sound of shattering glass and an asphyxiating cloud of chemicals flooding the car.

According to a new federal lawsuit and photos from the scene shared with The Intercept, federal agents smashed the car’s back windows and “sprayed the occupants with pepper spray through the lowered side windows.”

Officers then dragged a scared and temporarily blinded Roca Estrada from the car. “I was afraid they might be robbing me,” 24-year-old Roca Estrada told The Intercept through a translator. “They did not identify themselves. I was worried they were kidnapping me because they were asking very personal questions.”

“They did not identify themselves. I was worried they were kidnapping me.”

The June attack is one of six stories described in a lawsuit brought by several groups — including the American Civil Liberties Union of Virginia, the Washington Lawyers Committee for Civil Rights and Urban Affairs, the Legal Aid Justice Center, and multiple law firms — alleging widespread “unlawful and dangerous” warrantless arrests by immigration officials in Virginia.

On behalf of Roca Estrada and other plaintiffs, the groups are suing the Department of Homeland Security, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Acting Director of ICE David Venturella, and ICE D.C. Field Office Director Robert Guadian. They’re asking the court in the Eastern District of Virginia to force DHS to comply with congressional limits on warrantless immigration arrests and prohibit the agency from making immigration arrests without legally required individual assessments.

“They have a mandate from the Trump administration … to get creative and make arrests, however they see fit,” said Sophia Gregg, an immigrants’ rights attorney at the ACLU of Virginia. “The agents are ill-trained, and even when they do violate the law, there are no consequences.”
